questions.q: What is the order and degree of the differential equation: (d^2y/dx^2)^3 + dy/dx = sin(x)?
questions.explanation: The highest derivative is the second derivative (Order 2). Its power is 3 (Degree 3).

questions.q: What is the degree of the differential equation: d^2y/dx^2 + sin(dy/dx) = 0?
questions.explanation: Because a derivative (dy/dx) is the argument of the sine function, the equation is not a polynomial in its derivatives, so the degree is not defined.

questions.q: If a family of curves is given by y = A e^(2x) + B e^(-2x), what will be the order of its corresponding differential equation?
questions.explanation: There are two arbitrary constants (A and B), so the differential equation will be of order 2.

questions.q: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = y / x.
questions.explanation: Separate variables: dy/y = dx/x. Integrate: ln|y| = ln|x| + C'. Exponentiate: y = e^(ln|x| + C') = e^C' * x = C x.

questions.q: Find the integrating factor for the linear differential equation dy/dx + 3y = e^x.
questions.explanation: Here P(x) = 3. I.F. = e^(integral of 3 dx) = e^(3x).

questions.q: Find the integrating factor of x(dy/dx) - y = x^2.
questions.explanation: First divide by x: dy/dx - (1/x)y = x. Here P(x) = -1/x. I.F. = e^(integral of -1/x dx) = e^(-ln x) = e^(ln(x^-1)) = 1/x.

questions.q: The solution to a linear D.E. of the form dy/dx + Py = Q is given by:
options: y = integral of (Q * IF) dx + C
y * IF = integral of (Q * IF) dx + C
y * IF = integral of Q dx + C
y = IF * integral of Q dx + C
questions.explanation: This is the standard general solution formula for linear first-order differential equations.

questions.q: Is the differential equation dy/dx + x * y^2 = 0 a linear differential equation in y?
questions.explanation: No, because the dependent variable y is squared (y^2). A linear D.E. must have degree 1 for y and all its derivatives.
